name: The Ages of History, from Stone to Silicon
description: A guided tour through the named eras of the human story, from the first stone tools to the Information Age.

checkpoints.name: The long Stone Age
checkpoints.note: For millions of years our ancestors make stone tools, master fire and spread across the world as hunters and gatherers. Art appears in caves late in this age.

checkpoints.name: Farms, metals and first states
checkpoints.note: Farming creates villages and then cities. Bronze and later iron change tools and war, and the first states, writing and trade networks grow.

checkpoints.name: The classical world
checkpoints.note: Empires and philosophies spread from China to Rome. Greek culture reaches far under the Hellenistic kings, and Rome keeps order for centuries.

checkpoints.name: Middle Ages and golden ages
checkpoints.note: After Rome falls, new powers rise: Viking raiders, scholars of the Islamic world, Tang China, courts in Japan and the Church in Europe, and trade links the Old World.

checkpoints.name: The early modern world
checkpoints.note: Ships link the continents, printing helps the Reformation, new science changes ideas of nature, the Enlightenment questions kings, and Japan's Edo period and China's Qing dynasty keep large states in order.

checkpoints.name: Machines and empires
checkpoints.note: Factories and railways remake work, empires cover much of the globe, the Belle Epoque and the interwar years mark the end of the old order, and two world wars end it.

checkpoints.name: Atomic to information
checkpoints.note: Nuclear weapons, a Cold War, spaceflight and the computer give the modern world its shape, decolonisation redraws the map of Africa and Asia, and information becomes central to daily life.
